- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.03 to +0.37 in sentiment).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.40 to -0.50) or after sharp declines.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecasts by applying a 3-5 day moving average if sentiment volatility exceeds 0.30.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 30d forecast, check if sentiment was positive 2+ days prior — if so, reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly trending (e.g., -0.50+ for 3+ days); otherwise, assume 1–2 day lag in price correction.
